topicName: Redis Sentinel Architecture, Quorum, and Failover
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Redis Sentinel Architecture, Quorum, and Failover"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Redis Sentinel provides high availability for Redis without relying on external cluster managers. It monitors your master and replica instances, performs automatic failover if the master fails, and acts as a configuration provider for clients."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Core Architecture of Redis Sentinel"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A robust Redis Sentinel deployment typically consists of multiple Sentinel processes distributed across different virtual or physical machines. This distribution ensures that a single point of failure does not compromise the monitoring system itself. Sentinels communicate using a publish/subscribe mechanism and Redis commands to continuously check node health."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Monitoring: Sentinels constantly check if your master and replica instances are working as expected."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Notification: Sentinel can notify system administrators or other applications via an API that something is wrong with a Redis instance."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Automatic Failover: If a master is not working, Sentinel can start a failover process where a replica is promoted to master."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Configuration Provider: Sentinel acts as the authority for client discovery. Clients connect to Sentinels to ask for the address of the current master."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Quorum"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Quorum is the number of Sentinels that need to agree that the master is unreachable before taking action, such as triggering a failover. However, quorum is distinct from authorization. While a specific number of Sentinels (quorum) must detect a failure to start a failover, a majority of the total Sentinel instances must authorize the failover operation."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"sentinel monitor mymaster 127.0.0.1 6379 2"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"In the configuration snippet above, 'mymaster' is the master name, followed by its IP, port, and a quorum value of '2'. This means at least 2 Sentinels must agree that the master is down to initiate the failover workflow."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"The Failover Process"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"When a master goes offline, the failover process executes in several deterministic steps to ensure data consistency and minimal downtime."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"1. Failure Detection: A Sentinel marks a master as Subjectively Down (SDOWN) if it fails to respond to ping commands within a specified threshold (down-after-milliseconds)."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"2. Objective Down (ODOWN): When enough Sentinels (matching the configured quorum) independently report an SDOWN state within a timeframe, the master is marked as Objectively Down."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"3. Leader Election: A single Sentinel is elected to lead the failover process using the Raft-like leader election algorithm."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"4. Replica Promotion: The elected Sentinel selects the best replica based on criteria like replication offset, configuration priority, and run ID, then promotes it using the 'SLAVEOF NO ONE' command."},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Configuring Redis Sentinel"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"To set up a basic Sentinel configuration, create a sentinel.conf file with the mandatory parameters pointing to your master instance."},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"port 26379
sentinel monitor mymaster 192.168.1.100 6379 2
sentinel down-after-milliseconds mymaster 5000
sentinel failover-timeout mymaster 60000
sentinel parallel-syncs mymaster 1"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Always deploy a minimum of three Sentinel instances in production environments placed across separate failure domains to ensure a robust majority can be reached during network partitions."}]
